module.cms_data.checks: Detects WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento by content signatures (generator tag, readme, feeds), reads the version, and confirms exposures (XML-RPC, user enumeration) from content.
module.cms_data.fix:
Close the flagged exposures. XML-RPC (WordPress `/xmlrpc.php`): block it at the server (nginx and Apache snippets), unless a mobile app, Jetpack or a publishing tool uses it. User enumeration (`/wp-json/wp/v2/users`): reserve it for logged-in users (WordPress snippet, to place in a mu-plugin or in a child theme's `functions.php`).
Update the CMS, its themes and its plugins to the latest stable versions, after a backup. Delete unused themes and plugins: they remain attackable even when deactivated.
Hide the version: remove the `generator` tag from the page (WordPress: `remove_action('wp_head', 'wp_generator');`, in the snippet) and block web access to the files that describe the product (`readme.html`, `license.txt`, `README.txt`, `CHANGELOG.txt`, `RELEASE_NOTES.txt`). They are recreated at every update: prefer a server rule to a manual deletion.
The listed administration usernames are known to attackers: require long and unique passwords, enable two-factor authentication, limit sign-in attempts, and use a display name different from the login name. On WordPress, add `define('DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT', true);` to `wp-config.php` to forbid file editing from the administration.
For Drupal, Joomla and Magento: apply the security fixes published by the vendor, remove installation and documentation files from the server, and restrict the administration by IP address or VPN.
Check: `curl -s https://example.com/wp-json/wp/v2/users` must no longer list users, `curl -sI https://example.com/xmlrpc.php` must return `403`, and `curl -s https://example.com/ | grep -i generator` must no longer show a version. Then run the scan again.
module.cms_data.title: CMS fingerprint and exposures
module.cms_data.why: Knowing the CMS and its version maps the site to published flaws; open user enumeration or XML-RPC make credential attacks easier.
